text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: HIGH - inference-runtime errors on us-west-2 (5xx surge) :rotating_light:

olivia: seeing a big spike in 5xx from the model-runner pool in us-west-2. dashboards show ↑ error rate starting ~3925012300. TTLs/latency also up.

raj: confirmed. Gateway logs show many 502/504 and some 5xx with 'segfault' in runtime stderr.

mia: customer impact — support tickets from AcmePayments and EchoChat complaining about timeouts/failed responses. Acme flagged production traffic.

sam: can we get the exact error lines? I pulled a node log:

```
\n[model-runner-7] 2026-03-15T15:05:10Z ERROR runtime: segfault at 0x7fffa12c
[model-runner-7] stack: libinference.so(+0x5b4a2)
[model-runner-7] panic: double free near batch executor
[model-runner-7] 2026-03-15T15:05:11Z WARN evictor: OOM triggered, evicting kvcache entries
```

olivia: that matches the heap escalate traces I saw. Looks like a memory corruption followed by OOM and segfault cascade.

oncall-sre: I'm jumping in. Paging oncall to run live triage. @oncall-sre please confirm.

oncall-sre: oncall here. Initial plan: isolate failing model-runner pods, disable autoscale burst, and route traffic away from affected nodes.

raj: routing step: can we flip the smart-router policy to prefer us-west-1 and eu-west for new requests? We need to preserve low-latency customers but avoid us-west-2 hot nodes.

mia: do we have a canary/compatible fallback model variant? If we can fallback to a quantized smaller variant we can reduce memory pressure and keep requests alive.

sam: yes — model-id: gptx-large-v1-quant is compatible for many requests. I propose: 1) set router to prefer region fallback, 2) enable model-variant fallback to gptx-large-v1-quant for the impacted model tag, 3) cordon affected nodes and restart.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers: AcmePayments (ticket #3456), EchoChat (#7862) — ETA message drafted.

olivia: immediate mitigation actions being executed:
- routing change to prefer us-west-1/eu-west  (in progress)
- enable model-variant fallback to gptx-large-v1-quant  (in progress)
- cordon & recycle pods with segfaults  (in progress)

raj: applying k8s drain on runner nodes with segfaults now: `kubectl drain model-runner-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

sam: deploying fallback rule in router: PATCH /routing/policies 
payload:
```
{
  "model_tag": "gptx-v1-prod",
  "fallback_variant": "gptx-large-v1-quant",
  "prefer_regions": ["us-west-1","eu-west-1"],
  "max_retries": 1
}
```

olivia: small note — this will increase tokens cost a bit but preserves SLO. Acceptable tradeoff.

oncall-sre: restarted two nodes. Observed fewer segfault stack traces after restart, but still seeing evictions. Can we temporarily reduce batch sizes?

sam: changing executor batch size for the model to 64 -> 32 via runtime config: `PATCH /runtimes/gptx-v1/config { "max_batch": 32 }`

mia: support updated customers with the ETA and mitigation steps: "We have rerouted traffic and enabled a fallback variant. You may see slightly different latency and output formatting while we stabilize."

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0273 - Runtime 5xx surge (segfault + OOM) - page sent to oncall.

raj: monitoring key metrics: 5xx rate, kernel OOM counters, kvcache eviction rate, request latency p50/95.

olivia: quick metric snapshot (pre/post):
- 5xx rate: 14% -> 2.1% after routing changes
- kvcache evictions/min: 1200 -> 80
- p95 latency: 840ms -> 420ms

sam: looks like fallback + routing helped. still want to keep nodes cordoned for deeper forensics.

oncall-sre: starting core collection on the affected pod images and uploading to S3: `s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0273/cores/`

olivia: ops note: I captured a repro that seems to correlate with long-context prefix reuse + continuous KV cache growth. Could be a leak in kvcache eviction logic when combined with certain attention cache patterns.

mia: customer impact summary for the pager: AcmePayments — 24% of requests failed during surge window, EchoChat — intermittent timeouts, no data exfiltration. Both polite but urgent.

sam: next steps:
- postmortem runbook owner: olivia
- root cause: suspected memory corruption leading to OOM -> segfault (investigation ongoing)
- mitigation timeline: routing + fallback + restart completed by 3925012460
- followups: add additional kvcache telemetry, add guardrail to failover rather than try to use corrupted KV entries, add regression tests around long-prefix reuse.

olivia: assigning follow-ups in taskboard. I'll coordinate with eng-runtime to prepare a patch that hard-fails on suspicious kvcache growth.

oncall-sre: I'm leaving the incident. handoff to eng-runtime for deep-dive. On-call notes: keep the routing fallback for 2 hours and monitor.

raj: tagging: @eng-runtime @eng-ml @support.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned MILO postmortem backlog item: PM-INC-2026-0273.

mia: thanks team. I'll update Acme and EchoChat with a post-incident note once we have the RCA. :thumbsup:
